headline: AI startup Instinct raises $350M at $2.5B valuation for its viral AI assistant
summary: Founded just last year by a 23-year-old, Instinct's AI assistant helps organize users' lives, though it faces some privacy concerns regarding its permissions.
details: Instinct, a startup founded only last year by a 23-year-old, has secured $250 million in a Series B funding round. This latest investment brings its total funding to $350 million, valuing the company at $2.5 billion. The round was co-led by Index Ventures and Benchmark.

The company offers an AI assistant designed to efficiently organize users' lives by connecting to their apps and devices, communicating via texts and calls. Founder Noah Shinn highlighted user successes, including planning trips, buying groceries, and managing subscriptions.

Currently in private beta, Instinct has garnered enthusiasm from early users for its capabilities. However, the service has also sparked controversy due to privacy concerns, with users worried about the extensive permissions the app requires and the potentially invasive nature of its terms of use.

headline: Amazon Mechanical Turk shutting down September 30
summary: Amazon's long-running crowdsourcing platform, Mechanical Turk (MTurk), will cease operations on September 30, impacting a global workforce and businesses relying on its microtask services.
details: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) is a crowdsourcing marketplace that enables individuals and businesses to outsource tasks to a distributed, virtual workforce. These tasks range from simple data validation and research to more subjective jobs like survey participation and content moderation.

MTurk has been instrumental in harnessing collective intelligence and skills from a global workforce to streamline business processes, augment data collection, and accelerate machine learning development. It addresses tasks that humans perform more effectively than computers.

The platform allows for breaking down manual, time-consuming projects into smaller, manageable "microtasks" for distributed workers, offering a scalable solution. This helps companies manage labor costs and free up internal staff for higher-value activities.

Amazon has announced that its Mechanical Turk (MTurk) crowdsourcing platform will cease operations on September 30. This shutdown concludes a nearly two-decade run for a service that connected a global workforce with businesses needing human intelligence for various tasks.
